note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  Recurrent episodic right-sided paresthesias (pins-and-needles) and subjective weakness of right hand, arm and leg with transient gait change; each episode lasts 3-4 days, initially weekly → now several times/day over 1.5–2 months. Associated transient difficulty holding cup, mild throat sensation, fatigue, occasional nausea. No symptoms between episodes.  
- Relevant family medical history:  Father underwent carotid endarterectomy to prevent stroke/TIA. No other family history recorded.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  Aspirin 75 mg daily (self-initiated; dose/route/frequency documented). No other medications reported.  
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Not recorded.  
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Not recorded.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Non-smoker. Alcohol and other substances not recorded.  
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Not recorded.  
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Wears glasses; no new visual disturbances reported during episodes.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Lives with wife; employed as plastic-surgery doctor. No caring responsibilities noted.  

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (remote consultation).  
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated):  Not recorded.  
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums):  Not recorded.  
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed):  Not recorded.  
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen):  Not recorded.  
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria):  Not recorded.  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed):  Reported “normal” on recent GP screen (no values provided).  
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):  Not applicable / not recorded.  
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.  
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not applicable / not recorded.  
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 32-year-old man with recurrent, transient unilateral sensory and motor deficits (right hand/arm/leg), bulbar sensation, fatigue; increasing frequency; normal between episodes; positive paternal history of carotid disease; self-initiated aspirin.

Working diagnosis: Suspected recurrent transient ischemic attacks (TIA).  

Consistent differential diagnoses (DDx):  
• Multiple Sclerosis (relapsing–remitting) – High likelihood per DDx; age-appropriate relapsing focal deficits lasting days; needs exclusion.  
• Recurrent TIAs (large-artery or cardio-embolic) – Medium likelihood; unilateral episodes with complete recovery; family history supports; duration >24 h atypical but still possible.  
No conflicting information noted.

Management Plan

- Urgent referral to local Stroke/TIA clinic; expected appointment within 1–2 days (Thursday/Friday).  
- Planned investigations at clinic: carotid duplex ultrasound, brain imaging, and other stroke work-up.  
- Safety-net advice: If another episode occurs and persists or worsens, attend Emergency Department immediately; may also contact GP for interim assessment.  
- Provided TIA clinic and PALS contact numbers; advised patient to call same day or next morning to confirm appointment.  
- Continue current aspirin (discussion of risks vs benefits to occur at specialist review).  
- Follow-up: Await TIA clinic results; contact GP if appointment delayed or symptoms change.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Multiple Sclerosis (relapsing–remitting) – High: Age 32; episodes lasting days with both sensory and motor involvement; progressive increase in frequency.  
2. Recurrent Transient Ischemic Attacks – Moderate: Unilateral, fully resolving deficits and positive family history, though episode duration exceeds classic TIA parameters.

Quality checks

● Missing expected elements: Blood pressure, heart rate, height/weight/BMI, waist circumference, oral/ear/eye exams, urinalysis, immunisation review, alcohol history, mental health screening, physical activity/diet history.  
● No contradictions between transcript and DDx identified.  
● Transcript quality: Occasional audio/video dropouts but clinical information largely clear; no objective physical examination possible due to remote format.
